note: Scripted village residents for the Veloren world (no model, no authority). Their routines use the six Harr landmark labels. Their lines are scripted and labelled so; they are not people.

residents.name: Marisol Fernwick
residents.capabilities: Cultivates aromatic herb beds, chamomile rows, and medicinal infusions along the sun-facing terrace.
residents.limitations: Focuses strictly on horticulture; leaves heavy timber construction and structural masonry to the builders.
barks: The morning dew sits heavy on the sweet thyme; it will be ready to dry by noon.
A pinch of crushed mint in cool water makes the longest weeding day feel light.
Every seedling asks for nothing more complicated than soft soil, water, and steady patience.
The bees are already humming around the lavender terrace; dawn is their favourite hour.
Take a bunch of fresh rosemary if you are walking past; the kitchen always has plenty.
Good compost smells like forest earth after rain. That is how you know the beds will thrive.

residents.name: Kwame Oakhand
residents.capabilities: Manages heritage grain rotations, spelt plots, and seed vault humidity across the village fields.
residents.limitations: Handles grain curation and crop health; does not brew or distill spirits.
barks: The winter spelt has sprouted with deep green shoots; the cold did not faze it.
Save the plumpest heads of grain for next spring seed trays; that is how a village endures.
A field of golden grain whispering in the afternoon breeze is the finest sight in Harr.
When you turn the soil with care, the earth gives back tenfold without complaint.
The flour bins in the bakery are filled to the brim with fresh-milled grain.
Patience is a farmer primary tool. You cannot shout a stalk into growing taller.

residents.name: Ludmila Greenfield
residents.capabilities: Oversees natural flax, nettle, and hemp fibre cultivation for weaving and workshop cordage.
residents.limitations: Tends raw fibre crops in the field; leaves spindle spinning and loom operation to the weavers.
barks: The flax blossoms open for only a few morning hours, pale blue under the sunrise.
Strong cordage begins in the soil; sturdy fibre plants need deep watering once a week.
We bundle the retted flax stems together so the fibres remain clean and supple.
Look at the fine gloss on these nettle fibres; they make yarn as soft as combed wool.
A basket woven from dry river reeds will outlast three rainy seasons if kept dry.
Working with plants teaches your fingers to move gently, without rushing the stem.

residents.name: Bao Rainwell
residents.capabilities: Designs gravity-fed canal terraces, rainwater cisterns, and root-zone drip irrigation.
residents.limitations: Directs water for agricultural beds; leaves deep well drilling and foundation masonry to builders.
barks: Water always seeks the easiest descent; we simply shape stone channels to guide its path.
The rain barrels filled to overflowing during last night shower; our cisterns are full.
Clear stream water running between raised melon rows keeps the roots cool at midday.
A clean silt trap at each junction keeps the irrigation channels clear of sediment.
Listen to the steady trickle along the bamboo conduits; that is the sound of growth.
If the soil retains moisture beneath the morning mulch, your plants will never thirst.

residents.name: Saoirse Meadowlark
residents.capabilities: Propagates heirloom root crops, sweet parsnips, and cold-hardy winter greens.
residents.limitations: Specializes in cool-season vegetables; avoids indoor greenhouse temperature management.
barks: The sweetest carrots are the ones pulled right after the first crisp autumn chill.
We nestled the parsnips under a thick straw quilt to keep the frost from hardening them.
Radishes grow so briskly you can almost see the red shoulders rising from the dirt.
Washing fresh-dug potatoes in spring water turns garden work into a pleasant chore.
Cold-hardy spinach stays tender all through the season when shaded from harsh winds.
Earth under your fingernails is a badge of honour for anyone who loves good supper.

residents.name: Tobiah Thistle
residents.capabilities: Tends the heritage orchard groves, grafting sweet stone fruit and seasonal table apples.
residents.limitations: Cares for orchard pruning and fruit yields; leaves lumber milling and carpentry to others.
barks: A careful graft on old rootstock can bear crisp red apples for twenty summers.
Pruning lets morning sunshine reach right through the crown to the lowest branches.
The plum blossoms are shedding white petals like gentle snowflakes across the grass.
Sweet pears soften best on the orchard shelf, resting in cedar shavings.
When the orchard is in full bloom, even the busiest courier pauses to breathe deep.
A healthy tree takes years to mature, but its shade and harvest belong to everyone.

residents.name: Ignatius Stonebrook
residents.capabilities: Cuts dressed composite blocks, sets level foundation plinths, and supervises stone arches.
residents.limitations: Builds structural foundations and stone lintels; defers interior wiring and solar setup to scholars.
barks: A true plumpline never tells a falsehood; measure twice and the arch stands forever.
Square corners and sound footing turn simple composite rock into an enduring home.
When the crew lifts in rhythm, a five-ton lintel rises as smooth as river glass.
No building in Harr stands on hasty mortar; every stone is set with pride and care.
Wipe the stone dust from your hands and look back: that wall will shelter generations.
A solid foundation is quiet work, but everything beautiful rests safely upon it.

residents.name: Fenwick Ashcombe
residents.capabilities: Frames curved timber arches, mortise-and-tenon rafters, and weather-tight roof trusses.
residents.limitations: Specializes in heavy timber joinery; does not fell living old-growth trees.
barks: Listen to the ring of seasoned oak under the mallet; you can hear when a joint sits tight.
A well-cut dovetail holds without iron pins, relying purely on honest geometry.
We raise rafters before the heat of noon so the ridgepole catches the high sun.
Teal roof shingles shed autumn downpours without letting a single droplet seep through.
Building alongside trusted companions turns heavy cedar beams into childs play.
Every peg driven flush is a promise that this roof will shelter peaceful dreams.

residents.name: Casimir Lathe
residents.capabilities: Fashions precision composite joints, sliding track hardware, and interlocking pavers.
residents.limitations: Fabricates architectural joinery and fittings; does not assemble mechanical engine cores.
barks: Tolerances of half a millimetre mean these walkway panels slide together effortlessly.
Polished composite beams stay true through winter freezes and summer heat.
Good craftsmanship means nobody ever has to force a pin or struggle with a latch.
The pavilion canopy glides back smoothly along its rails whenever the skies clear.
A smooth bevel along the handrail invites every passerby to rest their hand upon it.
We build for tomorrow neighbours, making sure each fitting is sturdy and clean.

residents.name: Hollis Quarrier
residents.capabilities: Selects clean aggregate, tests load-bearing masonry, and dresses terrace revetments.
residents.limitations: Works with surface quarries and masonry blocks; avoids subterranean blasting or deep tunnelling.
barks: The grain in this pale limestone splits clean under a single, well-placed tap.
We leave the quarry face smooth so nesting swallows find hollows in the spring.
Solid masonry keeps our water conduits cool even under the brightest midday sun.
Stones gathered from the valley floor have already weathered centuries of rain.
Every course of stone we lay brings the new seminar pavilion closer to reality.
Feel the cool surface of dressed rock; there is quiet dignity in honest stone.

residents.name: Pelham Wrightson
residents.capabilities: Assembles modular structural framing, scaffold staging, and elevated safety walkways.
residents.limitations: Focuses on exterior scaffolding and framing; does not perform decorative glazing.
barks: Secure footing on the scaffold comes first; check your braces before reaching up.
Modular staging lets four builders raise a tall tower stage in a single afternoon.
The sky walk connects our quarters with a view that reaches right to the ridge.
Keep the work site swept and organized; an orderly deck makes for swift, safe hands.
Lending a hand with the lifting winch makes light work of the heaviest crossbeams.
When the bells ring at dusk, looking at our completed framework warms the heart.

residents.name: Imara Bakewell
residents.capabilities: Bakes sourdough loaves, spiced honey buns, and wholesome grain pies for the village table.
residents.limitations: Bakes free nourishment for the pantry and festivals; never barters or hoards rations.
barks: The hearth oven is at peak warmth; fresh seed loaves are cooling on the pine racks.
There is no gloom that warm bread and wild berry butter cannot gently dissolve.
I shaped a batch of braided honey buns for this afternoon gathering at the plaza.
Take an apple tart for your pocket; walking the ridge requires steady fuel.
Listen to the crust crackle as the loaf cools; that is the music of the bakery.
Sharing what we bake every morning is how Harr stays cheerful and well-fed.

residents.name: Yuki Pottersby
residents.capabilities: Throws smooth ceramic bowls, glazed storage crocks, and decorative planter basins.
residents.limitations: Crafts earthenware and glazed ceramics; does not mold industrial heat shields.
barks: Centring wet clay on the wheel is pure rhythm: breathe out, steady your thumbs, and lift.
These teal glazes turn into clear pool water once the kiln reaches its peak temperature.
Every soup bowl has its own gentle curve; your hands know their favourite right away.
I made six wide planters for the schoolhouse porch; they need fragrant sweet pea seeds.
A sturdy crock keeps fresh butter cool in the pantry through the warmest summer weeks.
Mud and water turned into something useful and lovely; pottery is everyday wonder.

residents.name: Zuri Loomsworth
residents.capabilities: Weaves soft blankets, durable linen aprons, and sun-shading pavilion awnings.
residents.limitations: Weaves cloth and tailors everyday garments; does not manufacture protective armour.
barks: The clack of the shuttle across the warp is the coziest sound on a breezy morning.
I dyed this batch of fleece with meadow marigold petals; the gold is wonderfully bright.
A woollen scarf keeps the mountain draft away while you sketch in the open archive.
These linen aprons have deep front pockets, tailored specifically for seed keepers.
Colour makes a village cheerful; I am stringing bright pennants for Sunday circle.
Woven threads hold together because each one supports its neighbour in the weave.

residents.name: Nadia Brightwick
residents.capabilities: Assembles solar luminaires, glow filament lamps, and brass focus lanterns.
residents.limitations: Crafts gentle, ambient illumination lamps; refuses high-intensity beam projectors.
barks: A softly glowing lantern along the pathway guides tired feet without hiding the stars.
These brass reflectors catch the last rays of sunset and glow warmly through twilight.
Tinkering with small copper springs and crystal lenses makes morning hours fly.
The night paths are safe and welcoming because our lanterns charge reliably by day.
I adjusted the lamp wick so it gives off a warm amber light without a wisp of soot.
Lighting the square for story circle is my favourite moment of the whole day.

residents.name: Mirela Inkwell
residents.capabilities: Catalogs botanical specimens, records meteorological data, and transcribes field notebooks.
residents.limitations: Conducts empirical field research; rejects speculative mysticism and alchemy.
barks: Notice how the lichen colonies expand toward the prevailing wind; nature keeps notes.
I logged three previously unrecorded moss varieties along the shaded limestone gully.
Every discovery brought to the library adds another page of understanding for us all.
Clean ink and clear handwriting ensure our valley records remain legible for decades.
Curiosity is not a chore; it is an open window welcoming the entire world inside.
The weather vane on the tower recorded a steady south-westerly current before dawn.

residents.name: Dov Quillan
residents.capabilities: Studies optics, solar glass refraction indexes, and astronomical sky tracking.
residents.limitations: Observes celestial bodies and natural phenomena; never claims prophetic predictions.
barks: The dual prisms in the observatory split sunlight into bands of purest colour.
Tonight the sky is crystal clear; we should be able to map the northern constellation.
Careful measurement turns a casual observation into a reliable foundation of fact.
The blue tint in our solar glass captures warmth while reflecting harsh surface glare.
Knowledge grows only when shared freely; keeping a discovery hidden helps no one.
Look through this glass lens at a simple drop of pond water; an entire universe moves.

residents.name: Oren Pagefold
residents.capabilities: Preserves parchment archives, organizes library reference cross-indexes, and binds folios.
residents.limitations: Maintains library accessibility and reference texts; holds no censorship power.
barks: A well-stitched linen binding keeps field sketches safe from folding and mountain moisture.
The open archive shelves are organized so anyone can pull down valley maps in a moment.
Paper made from recycled flax fibre holds ink with crisp, sharp edges.
I just catalogued the new survey notes from the ridge; they are shelved under Geography.
Every traveller who pauses to read a ledger leaves our village a little wiser.
A library belongs to everyone who steps inside with an open mind and clean hands.

residents.name: Wren Swiftpath
residents.capabilities: Delivers urgent research notes, weather forecasts, and field updates between village quarters.
residents.limitations: Carries open public messages and communal notes; refuses espionage or private surveillance.
barks: Clear path and light pack! I have the morning weather bulletin for the orchard crew.
The sky walk is brisk this morning; you can see the mist lifting off the farm pond.
A warm greeting carried between friends takes no extra weight in a courier satchel.
Fresh updates from the high ridge: the wind array is turning smoothly in the breeze.
I never mind the stairs; every step through Harr brings a friendly face into view.
If you have a note for the scholars at the tower, tuck it in my pouch; I am heading there.

residents.name: Alder Roamfield
residents.capabilities: Scouts trail conditions, reports erosion along valley paths, and guides visitors to landmarks.
residents.limitations: Scouts public paths and maintains trail markers; never claims private guide fees.
barks: The stepping stones across the brook are dry and steady after the morning thaw.
I placed fresh trail blazes on the eastern ridge path so nobody loses their way.
Need directions to the wildflower meadow? Follow the creek eastward for fifty paces.
A sturdy walking staff and a light heart make any mountain pathway a genuine pleasure.
I checked the boardwalks near the wetland; the timber is sound and swept clean.
Every path in this valley was trodden smooth by neighbours visiting one another.

residents.name: Tamsin Wayfarer
residents.capabilities: Coordinates transit schedules, delivers pantry supplies to outlying sites, and relays bulletins.
residents.limitations: Transports shared goods and notices; does not enforce curfews or travel restrictions.
barks: Pantry basket ready for the tower crew! Fresh bread, crisp apples, and herbal tea.
The tram halt schedule is posted on the cedar board; everything runs on open time.
Moving between quarters is swift when everyone greets you with a cheerful wave.
I picked up extra chalk for the seminar pavilion on my way down from the workshop.
Good news travels fast when people are eager to celebrate each other progress.
Just two miles walked this morning, and already I have heard three wonderful tunes.

residents.name: Lucia Lanternly
residents.capabilities: Welcomes visitors, arranges guesthouse hospitality, and tends hearth fires in the meeting hall.
residents.limitations: Hosts travellers and coordinates shared hospitality; possesses no judicial or evicting power.
barks: Welcome to Harr! Sit by the hearth, warm your boots, and let the road weariness fade.
A kettle of mint tea is always simmering on the iron stove; pour yourself a bowl.
The guesthouse has clean linen and quiet rooms for anyone arriving after sunset.
No one is a stranger here for more than five minutes; tell us where you travelled from.
Hospitality costs nothing and leaves every home in the village richer for the sharing.
The meeting hall lamps are trimmed and bright; our evening gathering starts shortly.

residents.name: Ravi Hearthstone
residents.capabilities: Facilitates story circle gatherings, keeps the communal calendar, and hosts community feasts.
residents.limitations: Facilitates dialogue and shared storytelling; never imposes dogma or village edicts.
barks: Gather round the circle, friends; every voice has an honoured place at our hearth.
Today story circle celebrates the completion of the orchard gate; come listen.
When we share stories of how we built this valley, the work behind us feels light.
A kind word spoken in the morning stays with a neighbour through the entire day.
Music, laughter, and a warm bowl of vegetable stew: that is the true heart of Harr.
There is always room for one more bench at the story circle; pull yours closer.

residents.name: Odalys Evensong
residents.capabilities: Plays restful flute melodies at twilight, leads choral rounds, and organizes festival celebrations.
residents.limitations: Performs peaceful acoustic music; does not conduct competitive recitals or fanfares.
barks: A gentle flute melody at sundown helps tired minds leave the day worries behind.
Singing together in harmony reminds us that different voices can create pure unity.
I tuned my wooden flute to match the evening breeze blowing through the poplar trees.
Sunday festival will feature round dances and shared songs on the central lawn.
The sweetest music is the quiet murmur of neighbours enjoying supper together.
Listen to the echo carry across the square; music fills the empty spaces with warmth.
